title: Capacity Runway & Price Coupling Playbook — May 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working playbook to align budget runway, headcount phasing, and pricing sensitivity for a potential mid-year demand spike. It blends a conservative runway target (18 weeks), a contractor-swap protocol for 8–24 week surges, and three price-tilt experiments to quantify elasticity and HC impact. Not final — testing assumptions and numbers with SRE/Platform next week.

Context / Why now:
- Recent inbound enterprise RFPs indicate ~2–3x token volume for promotional pilots starting Jul–Aug.
- Spot GPU mix is volatile; procurement can partially hedge via contractor/managed services in Q3.
- Need a quick decision grid for pricing moves vs hiring to preserve 20% gross margin target.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- ARR baseline (current run-rate): $75M implied annualized (as-of Apr 2026).
- Monthly hosted token demand baseline: 7B tokens/mo.
- Average unit cost per 1k tokens (baseline, blended): $0.012 (includes infra, model ops, amortized infra SRE).
- Avg revenue per 1k tokens (baseline): $0.035.
- Planned hires (net new) Q3 target: 12 FTEs across infra/eng/customer success if no price increases.
- Contractor cost premium: 1.8x equivalent FTE for short-term contractors; faster ramp (2–4 weeks).
- Runway target: cash buffer = 18 weeks of burn at plan midline.

Headcount phasing (working table):
- Format: Role | Jun | Jul | Aug | Sep | Oct | Nov | Notes
- Baseline FTEs hiring plan (no price change):
  - Infra Eng | 0 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 | slow ramp due to interview pipeline
  - Platform SRE | 0 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 | mix of junior/senior
  - Solutions Eng | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 | support pilot onboarding
  - Finance / Rev Ops | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | temporary revenue recognition support
- Contractor-swap plan (if demand surge >1.5x baseline):
  - Jun-Jul: convert 30% of planned FTE hires to contractors (pricing: +80% cost), reduces onboarding lag.
  - Aug-Sep: evaluate retention to FTE (target 40% hire-through) or wind down.

Budget snapshot (12-week focus; numbers illustrative):
- Monthly baseline burn (net of revenue): $5.2M
- Incremental burn per extra 1B tokens/mo (variable infra + ops): $14k/mo (net cost after efficiency maneuvers) — NOTE: this is per 1B, double-check with infra model.

Mini table (text) — projected monthly delta under surge scenarios:
- Columns: scenario | tokens/mo | incremental rev/mo | incremental cost/mo | incremental gross margin | net cash burn delta
- Baseline | 7B | $245k | $84k | $161k | -$0.0M
- Surge A (x1.5) | 10.5B | $367.5k | $126k | $241.5k | -$0.12M (contractor mix)
- Surge B (x2.0) | 14B | $490k | $168k | $322k | -$0.30M (mix heavy contractors)

Pricing sensitivity experiments (three quick levers):
- Experimental design: simulate immediate price tilt on new customers only (pilot cohort) vs platform-wide price step. Run elasticities using historical uptake from Jan–Apr 2026 paywalls.
- Price experiments:
  - Tilt 1: +10% unit price to new tiers -> expected demand elasticity: -6% to -10% (conservative: -8%)
  - Tilt 2: +20% unit price + small feature gating (rate limits for free tiers) -> expected elasticity: -12% to -18% (conservative: -15%)
  - Tilt 3: +30% across-the-board -> expected elasticity: -25% to -35% (conservative: -30%)
- Quick sensitivity outputs (conservative elasticity numbers):
  - +10% price -> revenue per 1k tokens becomes $0.0385; net revenue change (assuming -8% volume) ~ +1.5% overall; reduces immediate HC need by ~1–2 hires (Q3)
  - +20% price -> revenue per 1k tokens $0.042; net revenue change (assuming -15% volume) ~ +2.6%; reduces HC need by ~3–5 hires (Q3)
  - +30% price -> revenue per 1k tokens $0.0455; net revenue change (assuming -30% volume) ~ -3.5% (negative); increases churn risk for low-touch customers — not recommended wholesale

Break-even calculus (simple):
- Cost of 1 FTE fully loaded (avg across roles): $28k/mo (comp + benefits + infra).
- Equivalent contractor cost for same output: $50k/mo.
- If price increase yields >=$28k/mo incremental gross (per hire replaced), then hiring vs contractor decision flips. Use this to justify contractor-swap for first 3 months of surge.

Risk matrix (short):
- Risk: rapid churn among SMBs if tilt >20% -> Mitigation: targeted cohorts and grandfathering, feature-led price tiers.
- Risk: spot GPU cost spikes -> Mitigation: expand reserved capacity for critical models; shift noncritical workloads to quantized variants.
- Risk: hiring pipeline stalls -> Mitigation: prioritize contractor-swap + cross-functional on-call incentives.

Open questions for review meeting (May 12):
- Confirm infra incremental cost per 1B tokens with infra cost model (Sashi to verify).
- Legal: contractor conversion agreements + IP (Lina to loop).
- Sales: willingness to accept pilot price tilts for enterprise prospects (Aaron to confirm with top 5 pipeline accounts).

Decision knobs (recommended near-term):
- Move 30% of planned Q3 hires to contractor-swap until demand clears (approve up to $300k incremental cash for contractor premiums in Q3).
- Launch Tilt 1 (+10% new-customer pricing) targeted at pilot enterprise cohorts starting Jul 1 for 12 weeks, measure conversion & token consumption delta.
- Create automated dashboard (Console finance view) for token burn vs gross margin by customer cohort; daily refresh for first 8 weeks of pilot.

Short action list (owner tags):
- Sashi: validate incremental infra cost per 1B tokens by May 8.
- Aaron: confirm pilot cohort willingness and list of 5 customers by May 9.
- Lina + Legal: draft short-term contractor conversion term sheet by May 14.
- Jamal: build quick dashboard prototype (Cohort + tokens + revenue + margin) by May 20.

Appendix: sensitivity snapshot (raw numbers for modeling)
- Baseline monthly tokens: 7,000,000,000
- Revenue per 1k tokens baseline: $0.035 -> baseline rev/mo = (7,000,000k * 0.035) = $245k
- Cost per 1k tokens baseline: $0.012 -> baseline cost/mo = (7,000,000k * 0.012) = $84k
- Elasticity caveat: derived from internal pricing cohort A (Nov 2025–Mar 2026); small-n; confidence = low

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally leaves gaps (checkpoints) so finance/infra/product can insert validated numbers. Think of it as an operations-ready working brief rather than polished analysis.
- Please annotate the confluence link with verified infra deltas and any legal flags so we can finalize by May 18.

End of playbook (working draft).
